A black hole the mass of the moon would have an event horizon about the size of a sand grain. Since the moon's mass and position wouldn't change, the Earth's motion and tides wouldn't

change either. Our black hole moon would be pretty low profile. If it were much smaller, it would evaporate through Hawking radiation. But a black hole the mass of the moon actually absorbs more energy from the cosmic background radiation t
If the black hole devoured any objects, it would let off a tremendous blast of radiation. Black hole accretion disks are one of the most efficient ways to convert mass into energy in

the universe. Fortunately, there's not a lot out there for the black hole moon to eat, so it wouldn't glow very brightly for now. It would spend most of its time drastically altering the orbits of nearby dust particles, one sand grain pushi
All in all, the conversion of the moon to a black hole might not be that big of a deal.
